milestone: First DemoBoard boards delivered and tested

stop.set_by: a loop guard, not a plan of work

adopted.shape: A stored position per track. Each node ends with one outcome, and the outcome names where to go. A stage is a row of nodes; a stage is passed when its last node passes.

stay_outcomes.more_work: stay; continue the same task under its agreed stop
stay_outcomes.needs_owner: stay; present the concrete decision to the owner with a recommendation
stay_outcomes.needs_lead: stay; the lead inspects the obstacle and helps
stay_outcomes.needs_skill: stay; practice the missing operation on the research track, then return

move_outcomes.pass: move to the node this node's pass names; done when it names done
move_outcomes.returned: a finding sends work back to one of the nodes this node's returned list allows

rules: Position is the target of the last transition on the track. With no transition, position is the track's start.
A node cannot pass while an open issue names it in close_before.
A node with requires cannot pass until each named node has a pass transition.
Framework nodes are a list, not a row: their transitions never move a track's position.

A node with unchanged_pass passes by itself when its view of the board (placement: the footprints' references, library footprints, sides and positions; copper_and_silk: the board without its part fields) is the one at its last pass: next records the pass as script:unchanged before starting the card, an owner's card included, since the owner's pass on the same view stands. A node a returned record sent work back to does not pass by itself until it records a pass of its own after that return.

tracks.label: Routing research (a side trip from Routing batch)

nodes.label: Inventory
nodes.task: Read the saved schematic, board, rules and BOM. This proves inventory only, not ERC, DRC or hardware performance.
nodes.pass_when: The saved schematic, board, rules and BOM read cleanly.

nodes.label: Decisions
nodes.task: Record the owner's product and board decisions for this revision in board/DECISIONS.md, in the owner's words. Each open issue names the node it must close before.
nodes.pass_when: The decisions for this revision are written, and every open issue names where it closes.

nodes.label: Constraints
nodes.task: Review the circuit, datasheets and firmware interface settings against the electrical contract and the decisions. Justify spacing, return paths, bus timing, decoupling and power widths; separate source-backed requirements from local choices. Define the first routing batch: its nets, method and stop.
nodes.pass_when: The electrical contract (R1 to R14) is current for this revision, and the first routing batch is defined with nets, method and stop.

nodes.label: Schematic
nodes.task: The parts and connections. Keep the schematic the source: the board is updated from it. Render the pages and run the schematic critic; resolve each finding or decline it with a reason.
nodes.pass_when: ERC reports 0 errors and 0 warnings; schematic critic findings are resolved; the pages read cleanly: signal left to right, power up, ground down, net labels instead of long crossing wires.

nodes.label: BOM
nodes.task: An exact part for every schematic part: manufacturer, MPN and supplier identity agree across the schematic, the board and the exported BOM, each board part's LCSC Part # names the part its Supplier Part names, and every approved target is fitted. Validate every row and factory/manual/DNP/off-board boundary, including mechanical-footprint exclusions and owner-soldered through-hole joints on SMT parts.
nodes.pass_when: Schematic, board and exported BOM name the same parts; every approved target is fitted with its selected manufacturer, MPN and supplier; no identity or consistency findings.

nodes.label: Stock
nodes.task: Can the factory supply those exact parts. Record dated listings for every factory part: listed manufacturer, MPN, supplier ID, class, stock and price. For a shortage or preorder, record the owner's accepted plan in the owner's words; a plan is not confirmed fulfillment.
nodes.pass_when: A dated listing exists for every factory part, at most 30 days old; every shortage has a plan the owner accepted.

nodes.label: Datasheets
nodes.task: Every BOM part has its datasheet in hardware/reference and its package and height taken from it into hardware/reference/parts.json.
nodes.pass_when: Every BOM part is in parts.json with a datasheet on hand and a height taken from it.

nodes.label: Models
nodes.task: Every part's 3D model loads, and its top matches the datasheet height. Make or check the model against the datasheet.
nodes.pass_when: Every part's 3D model loads and its top is within 0.3 mm of the datasheet height.

nodes.label: Footprints
nodes.task: Every board footprint is identical to its library copy, and the library holds nothing the board does not use. Every joint soldered by hand is shown buildable from the maker's data by scripts/board_manual_joints.py, which writes board/reports/footprints/manual_joints.md: the real pin, from its datasheet in hardware/reference/parts.json, passes the smallest finished hole, or the hole is as the maker draws it; the pad has a mask opening on both faces; it joins no plane solid. A joint with neither a pin nor a maker's hole on record is not proven and keeps this card open. A repair changes only what the finding names.
nodes.pass_when: Every board footprint matches its library copy; the library has no unused footprint; DRC's accepted library-mismatch list is empty; every hand-soldered joint fits its pin or is as the maker draws it, has mask openings and thermal relief, and none is unproven.

nodes.label: Placement
nodes.task: Compare recorded footprint positions, rotations and sides with the owner's approved placement, render the views, and get the owner's approval on a rendered view. The approval covers which way each part faces, so before asking, look at every part with a direction on the rendered view: connectors toward their edge or their mate, keys, indicators and controls, pin 1 and polarity marks. Changed placement needs a new approval; never route ahead of it.
nodes.pass_when: Recorded positions, rotations and sides match board/owner_placement.json, and the owner has approved the rendered view.

nodes.label: Routing batch
nodes.task: Start from the latest incoming graph record and its evidence to define this visit. On a review return, first inspect its findings without editing copper: separate accepted geometry and checker artifacts, repair checker defects, and bring conflicting rules or owner tradeoffs to the owner with a recommendation and cost. Define the next bounded copper batch only after those dispositions and owner authorization. Work in the KiCad editor. Write each connection of the batch as a text file in one folder on the board branch and commit it; then `py -3 scripts/routing_run.py <folder> --by <who>` runs them as locked editor steps, adopts the board when only tracks, arcs and vias changed, commits it with the step lines and records more_work or needs_lead with its tokens. Before a copper batch, its nets must be clear of open issues. That run is the only way copper is laid: never write tracks, vias or pours with a script or through KiCad's programming interface, never use another router, and never run the route tool by hand outside the run. When the run cannot lay a connection, record needs_lead with what the route tool said and stop; the card refuses pass and more_work while the board holds copper that no run committed. Refill zones and save. Run the copper diff against origin/main with the batch nets, declaring each change to earlier copper or part positions as a fix with its reason. Render and inspect the pictures. Run fresh saved-fill, DRC/parity, route-quality, electrical, pad-mask, thermal-relief, hand-solder-joint and exhaustive checks and the relevant track-craft checks. Resolve or explain each finding and obtain the targeted board critic. Record more_work with the batch nets until the whole board is routed. Preserve accepted placements, labels and waivers unless the owner changes that decision.
nodes.pass_when: All intended connections are routed; saved-state connectivity, return paths and relevant checks inspected on the current revision.

nodes.label: Board checks
nodes.task: Read CI's validate run for this commit from its board-checks artifact: scripts/validate_board.py as the runner executed it (ERC, DRC with schematic parity, saved fills, route quality, electrical audit, pad mask, thermal relief on through-hole pads, the hand-soldered joints, the full audit and routing progress). A run that allowed an unfinished board, inherited a failure from its base or skipped the checks as an incremental change is not a pass.
nodes.pass_when: Every check passes on this revision with no inherited or unfinished-board allowance.

nodes.label: Visual review
nodes.task: Render the board views and run the board critic against the exact files and pictures. Run tools/kicad/check_track_craft.py with --output board/reports/visual_review/track-craft.json for track-craft rules and inspect what each view shows. Resolve each finding or decline it with a one-line reason; owner tradeoffs go to the owner.
nodes.pass_when: Board critic findings on the rendered views are resolved or declined with a reason.

nodes.label: Verification
nodes.task: Reconcile active contracts, scripts and critic rubrics against the finished design. Close every open issue that names this node. Run fresh checks and stamp every report against this board's hash. An independent review reproduces the checks from the files, not the reports.
nodes.pass_when: Every open issue naming verification is closed; all reports are fresh against this board's hash; the independent review reproduces the checks.

nodes.label: Package
nodes.task: Generate Gerbers, drills, BOM, CPL and the manual assembly list from one saved revision and the selected assembly scope into board/production. Regenerate reports; never relabel old ones current. Hash the exact release archive.
nodes.pass_when: Order package gates G1 to G10 and G12 pass; the exact archive and its evidence are attached.

nodes.label: Orientation preview
nodes.task: Gate G11: the owner looks at the assembler's placement preview for every polarized or orientation-sensitive part and writes the result in board/DECISIONS.md with the date.
nodes.pass_when: The owner has written the preview result for every polarized part in DECISIONS with the date.

nodes.label: Quote
nodes.task: Refresh stock for the final BOM. Obtain quotes at each service level the assembler offers for the same board, quantity and assembly scope, itemized as PCB fabrication, components, setup and stencil, feeder loading, minimum quantities and attrition, SMT assembly, through-hole or hand assembly, special inspection or processes, sourcing or consignment, and shipping and taxes. Show total delivered cost and the incremental cost of fuller assembly. Run docs/BOARD_ORDER_COMMON_SENSE_CHECKLIST.md on the final files; the owner chooses assembly scope and quantity.
nodes.pass_when: Stock is current for the final BOM; quotes are itemized; the checklist passes with direct evidence; the owner has chosen assembly scope and quantity.

nodes.label: Order
nodes.task: Present the exact files, quantity, total cost, manual work and known tradeoffs. List what the owner buys apart from the factory order, set against the parts on hand in board/DECISIONS.md, plus bench bring-up supplies and loads. Place the order only with the owner's explicit authorization.
nodes.pass_when: The owner authorized; the order number, quantity, cost and supplier confirmation are recorded.

nodes.label: Delivery
nodes.task: Receive the boards. Record quantities and the incoming inspection against the ordered revision (acceptance run, section 1).
nodes.pass_when: Boards received; incoming discrepancies resolved or explicitly carried into bench work.

nodes.label: Assembly
nodes.task: Per unit: unpowered electrical gate, dry fit, manual soldering in order, post-solder unpowered gate (acceptance run, sections 2 to 5). Any remaining assembly from the selected factory scope, including mechanical mounting.
nodes.pass_when: Sections 2 to 5 are recorded for each identified unit.

nodes.label: First power
nodes.task: First-power steps of the acceptance run, in order: current-limited first power with no sensitive load fitted, supply rail verification, and safe initial bring-up gate.
nodes.pass_when: First-power steps are recorded for each unit with the prepared firmware build named.

nodes.label: Subsystems
nodes.task: Subsystem bring-up: display, storage, serial, USB, controls and sensor input, alone and all at once. Measure timing latency, jitter and noise floor with bench instruments against baseline criteria.
nodes.pass_when: Measured evidence for power, latency, jitter, display, storage, serial, USB, controls and sensor input is recorded for the received units and the exact firmware binary; outstanding failures remain explicit.

nodes.label: Product judgment
nodes.task: Final enclosure gate, real functional evaluation on the finished product, and assembly repeatability check. Bench performance numbers are measured, never judged by feel.
nodes.pass_when: The owner's product judgments are recorded for the received units.

nodes.label: Firmware ready
nodes.task: Prepare the firmware build for the controller and carrier: display, storage, serial, controls and sensor coverage. Check pin ownership against the routed netlist; a conflict returns to the design before any order. Record source_revision, build_target and the exact binary. Flashing or taking hardware needs owner authorization.
nodes.pass_when: A reproducible carrier-specific build, checked pin ownership and an executable first-board test procedure are ready, with equipment and coverage stated.

nodes.label: Long-lead parts
nodes.task: Pre-order long-lead IC stock in the owner's assembler account as a backup if factory reel stock fluctuates. Record the order number, date paid and delivery estimate.
nodes.pass_when: Long-lead parts are reserved in the owner's assembler parts inventory.

nodes.label: Enclosure spacer
nodes.task: Model and test a mechanical spacer that aligns with the board mounting holes without contacting copper or parts.
nodes.pass_when: The spacer fits cleanly into the first board by hand without rocking or touching copper or parts.

nodes.label: IPC research and router survey
nodes.task: Selectively inspect official KiCad IPC documentation and examples, relevant skills and router candidates. Compare capabilities, limits, platform and version support, licenses and publisher trust. Follow the third-party tool rule before adoption or execution.
nodes.pass_when: Source-linked IPC findings and an initial router survey identify useful candidates, known limitations, untested claims and bounded next experiments.

nodes.label: IPC routing challenge
nodes.task: On a disposable copy of a multi-connection benchmark fixture, test the stated IPC or hybrid method. Compare against interactive routing from the same starting state. Count lead help, retries, elapsed time and model usage; mark missing usage unknown.
nodes.pass_when: All benchmark connections are repaired and assessed against the matching starting state, with assistance, checks, quality, costs and limitations recorded.

nodes.label: Router comparison
nodes.task: Compare KiCad's interactive router, external engines and hybrid IPC approaches: constraints, layers, preservation on import, control, licensing, known failures and total effort. Run vetted candidates on disposable cases within an agreed scope.
nodes.pass_when: An evidence-linked comparison, including bounded trials and their limits, explains when each approach applies.

nodes.label: Graph execution adapters
nodes.task: Connect demonstrated scripts, editor operations, targeted reviews and inspected pictures to graph transitions. Bounded execution, stops that end a loop, retry limits and lead-assisted recovery. Preserve owner decisions for parts, placement, tradeoffs and purchasing.
nodes.pass_when: Representative operations and failure paths run through the graph with observed artifacts and enforced stops.

nodes.label: Token use
nodes.task: Connect provider and session usage capture to graph transitions. Include lead, workers, reviews, retries and failures; separate tokens by model, elapsed time, human help, development versus repeat runs, and what was repeated, refused or redone.
nodes.pass_when: A complete demonstrated task has traceable usage for all contributors, explicit missing coverage, and a reproducible comparison of token use and result quality.

nodes.label: Shared progress and evidence retention
nodes.task: Make graph state and accepted evidence durable across workstation, KiCad host and account handoff. Keep required fixtures, costs and proof; archive bulky captures; retire redundant scratch and old worktrees only after checking open work.
nodes.pass_when: A cross-machine handoff restores current state and evidence correctly; retention choices are resolved without losing active work or measurement baselines.

nodes.label: Board graph as its own tool
nodes.task: Keep the board graph engine in its own repository that multiple board projects install or pin, reading per-board descriptions and site settings with no project-specific paths.
nodes.pass_when: Multiple projects run their board cards from the shared tool repository with clean verification.

open_issues.issue: The controller module datasheet publishes neither a pin size nor a hole size, so the Footprints card's joint check cannot prove its forty joints. Measure one pin of a module on hand against the board's 1.1 mm holes (1.02 mm smallest finished; an ordinary 0.64 mm square pin is 0.905 mm corner to corner), and put the measurement in hardware/reference/parts.json.
Complete first-article firmware bring-up and bench diagnostics in docs/ACCEPTANCE_RUN.md, including display, storage, serial, USB, controls and sensor threshold calibration.
Measure the installed controller module stack height with calipers before releasing the enclosure model.
The debug header (J6) and its jumper (JP3) are not fitted on the first article. Before anyone fits them, check their mating dimensions against the maker's drawing.
